newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ashton wants Argyle expansion to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Ashton wants Argyle expansion to go ahead.

text.p: Australia's Ashton Mining Ltd expressed confidence on Tuesday its 40.1 percent owned Argyle diamond mine would be expanded beyond year 2003.
"There will be some form of expansion. Quite how it is configured remains to be determined," Ashton chief executive John Robinson told the company's annual meeting in Melbourne.
Mining giant RTZ-CRA owns the other 59.9 percent of the diamond mine, the world's biggest, and has yet to make a formal joint venture decision with Ashton on its future.
The mine life of the current pit design ends around year 2003. Argyle produces around 40 million carats a year.
Ashton is considering a combination of open pit and underground expansion plans. It expects to make a decision on expansion by the middle of calendar 1997.
Robinson said Ashton would probably go ahead with an expansion even if RTZ-CRA did not wish to do so.
"I think we probably would but obviously that's an issue that would have to be discussed in some detail and it's too early to make that sort of decision," he told reporters.
"Until we know exactly what the RTZ beyond-life is, it would be silly to reflect on that," he said.
